title: Abstract Classes and Methods knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly distinguishes TypeScript access modifiers and JavaScript private fields?
options: JavaScript #private fields are comments removed before execution.
TypeScript private is primarily a type-checking restriction; JavaScript #private fields enforce runtime privacy.
Both mechanisms are identical in all runtime behavior.
questions.answer_key: TypeScript private is primarily a type-checking restriction; JavaScript #private fields enforce runtime privacy.
questions.explanation: Runtime behavior matters when selecting an encapsulation mechanism.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Abstract Classes and Methods”?
options: The concept should be demonstrated with abstract base classes and checked against its intended contract.
The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with abstract base classes and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Abstract base classes”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Abstract Classes and Methods”?
options: Assume comparing abstract classes with interfaces is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check required subclass behavior, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.answer_key: Check required subclass behavior, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Required subclass behavior”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
